problem: Diffusion-based mapless visual navigation policies (e.g., NavDP) need many denoising steps and so have high latency, and behavior cloning caps performance at expert quality. Naively cutting to one or few generation steps makes trajectories head straight to the goal and ignore obstacles.
motivation: Real-time deployment on resource-limited robots needs low-latency planning, yet few-step generation degrades obstacle avoidance because the trajectory gets few chances to attend to spatial structure. RL fine-tuning of generative policies can go beyond the imitation ceiling and adapt to a target embodiment.
key_idea: Combine few-step (5-step) MeanFlow trajectory generation with critic-gradient refinement of the intermediate trajectory (CGTR) and an obstacle proximity auxiliary task, then adapt the policy with PPO plus BC regularization and critic updates.
insight: The few-step quality loss comes mainly from missing obstacle awareness, and a critic trained on point-cloud-derived scores can fix it cheaply: with CGTR, 5-step reaches 59.4% SR, matching 10-step without CGTR (59.2%) at about 10 ms overhead. Ablations show removing CGTR causes the largest drop (-13.5 SR), then OPP (-9.0) and RL fine-tuning (-7.5). BC regularization mainly protects SPL (removing it reduces average SPL by 7.4 points). Single-step CGTR is best, since 3 steps over-correct.
method: MeanFlow policy: Transformer policy predicts average velocity u(z,r,t,h). It is trained with a MeanFlow loss using JVP and integrated in T=5 steps at inference (NavDP is 10 steps).
Multi-modal encoder: two DINOv2 ViT-S encoders (history RGB, current depth replicated to 3 channels), fused by a lightweight Transformer decoder into h_cond.
Obstacle Proximity Prediction (OPP): auxiliary MLP predicts the min obstacle distance in each of 12 angular sectors, supervised by the dataset point cloud with SmoothL1. It is removed at inference.

Critic head: shares the decoder and scores trajectories as -λc·(fraction of waypoints within d_safe of obstacles)+λg·goal progress (λc=5, λg=0.1). It is trained by MSE on expert and perturbed trajectories and ranks N candidates at inference.
CGTR: at the penultimate denoising step, z ← z + η·Clip(∇_z C, δ) with η=0.4, δ=1.0, one guidance step, inspired by classifier guidance.

PPO fine-tuning in sim: Gaussian noise is injected in the last flow steps, and the CGTR correction is included in the log-prob. Dense reward: β_p=5 progress, β_s=50 ESDF safety, β_g=20 goal bonus within 0.5 m. Loss is L_PPO + λ_BC·L_BC (to a frozen reference policy) + λ·L_C, so the critic is updated during Stage 2.

setting.backbone: MeanFlow Transformer policy + critic with DINOv2 ViT-S RGB and depth encoders (pre-trained, then PPO fine-tuned)
setting.training_data: Stage 1: NavDP-style expert trajectory data (InternVLA-N1/NavDP benchmark setting) with obstacle point clouds, 8×A800 for 24 h. Stage 2: PPO in an InternUtopia indoor environment in IsaacSim, 1×RTX 4090 for 12 h.
setting.observation: history RGB frames + current depth image + point goal
setting.action_space: predicted trajectory of future waypoints (local planner)
setting.privileged: Training-time only: obstacle point clouds and ESDF for critic/OPP supervision and reward. None at test time.

numbers.extra: matched-compute retrained baselines; SR within 1 m; latency 60 ms on RTX 4090

numbers.eval_set_note: 100 indoor scenes, Easy and Hard settings
10 trials each in Easy indoor, Outdoor, Hard indoor

numbers_note: Not a standard VLN benchmark; results are on the NavDP/InternVLA-N1 point-goal benchmark. Denoising-step and eta sweeps are given only in figures, with a few values in the text.
results: On the NavDP point-goal benchmark under matched compute, NavCMPO reaches 74.7 SR / 65.1 SPL average vs 68.3 / 60.3 for retrained NavDP (+6.4 SR, +4.8 SPL), with latency cut from 85 to 60 ms. On the real Go2 it reaches 66.7% average SR vs 56.7% for NavDP and 33.3% for ViPlanner.
limitations: Matched-compute comparison against a retrained NavDP only; it does not claim to beat the original NavDP, and the same RL fine-tuning is not applied to NavDP.
Single real-robot embodiment (Go2) and only 10 trials per scenario; RL adaptation is done in simulation only.
Not the fastest: the one-step MP1 runs at 30 ms, and ViPlanner at 30 ms.
